texts.hos.4.12: My people at its staff asketh and its rod declareth to it, For a spirit of whoredoms hath caused to err, And they go a-whoring from under their God.
texts.hos.4.13: On tops of the mountains they do sacrifice, And on the hills they make perfume, Under oak, and poplar, and terebinth, For good [is] its shade.
texts.hos.4.14: Therefore commit whoredom do your daughters, And your spouses commit adultery, I do not see after your daughters when they commit whoredom, And after your spouses when they commit adultery, For they with the harlots are separated, And with the whores they do sacrifice, A people that doth not understand kicketh.
texts.hos.4.15: Though a harlot thou [art], O Israel, Let not Judah become guilty, And come not ye in to Gilgal, nor go up to Beth-Aven, Nor swear ye, Jehovah liveth.
texts.hos.4.16: For as a refractory heifer hath Israel turned aside, Now doth Jehovah feed them as a lamb in a large place.
texts.hos.4.17: Joined to idols [is] Ephraim, let him alone.
texts.hos.4.18: Sour [is] their drink, They have gone diligently a-whoring, Her protectors have loved shame thoroughly.
texts.hos.4.19: Distressed her hath wind with its wings, And they are ashamed of their sacrifices!
texts.hos.5.1: `Hear this, O priests, and attend, O house of Israel, And, O house of the king, give ear, For the judgment [is] for you, For, a snare ye have been on Mizpah, And a net spread out on Tabor.
texts.hos.5.2: And to slaughter sinners have gone deep, And I [am] a fetter to them all.
texts.hos.5.3: I have known Ephraim, And Israel hath not been hid from me, For now thou hast gone a-whoring, Ephraim, Defiled is Israel.
texts.hos.5.4: They give not up their habitual doings, To turn back unto their God, For a spirit of whoredoms [is] in their midst, And Jehovah they have not known.
texts.hos.5.5: And humbled hath been the excellency of Israel to his face, And Israel and Ephraim stumble by their iniquity, Stumbled also hath Judah with them.
texts.hos.5.6: With their flock and with their herd, They go to seek Jehovah, and do not find, He hath withdrawn from them.
texts.hos.5.7: Against Jehovah they dealt treacherously, For strange sons they have begotten, Now consume them doth a month [with] their portions.
texts.hos.5.8: Blow ye a cornet in Gibeah, a trumpet in Ramah, Shout, O Beth-Aven, after thee, O Benjamin.
texts.hos.5.9: Ephraim is for a desolation in a day of reproof, Among the tribes of Israel I have made known a sure thing.
texts.hos.5.10: Princes of Judah have been as those removing a border, On them I do pour out as water My wrath.
texts.hos.5.11: Oppressed is Ephraim, broken in judgment, When he pleased he went after the command.
texts.hos.5.12: And I [am] as a moth to Ephraim, And as a rotten thing to the house of Judah.
texts.hos.5.13: And see doth Ephraim his sickness, and Judah his wound, And Ephraim goeth unto Asshur, And sendeth unto a warlike king, And he is not able to give healing to you, Nor doth he remove from you a scar.
texts.hos.5.14: For I [am] as a lion to Ephraim, And as a young lion to the house of Judah, I -- I tear and go, I bear away, and there is no deliverer.
texts.hos.5.15: I go -- I turn back unto My place, Till that they are desolate, and have sought My face. In their distress they do seek Me speedily!'
texts.hos.6.1: `Come, and we turn back unto Jehovah, For He hath torn, and He doth heal us, He doth smite, and He bindeth us up.
texts.hos.6.2: He doth revive us after two days, In the third day He doth raise us up, And we live before Him.
texts.hos.6.3: And we know -- we pursue to know Jehovah, As the dawn prepared is His going forth, And He cometh in as a shower to us, As gathered rain -- sprinkling earth.'
texts.hos.6.4: What do I do to thee, O Ephraim? What do I do to thee, O Judah? Your goodness [is] as a cloud of the morning, And as dew rising early -- going.
texts.hos.6.5: Therefore I have hewed by prophets, I have slain them by sayings of My mouth, And My judgments to the light goeth forth.
texts.hos.6.6: For kindness I desired, and not sacrifice, And a knowledge of God above burnt-offerings.
texts.hos.6.7: And they, as Adam, transgressed a covenant, There they dealt treacherously against me.
texts.hos.6.8: Gilead [is] a city of workers of iniquity, Slippery from blood.
texts.hos.6.9: And as bands do wait for a man, A company of priests do murder -- the way to Shechem, For wickedness they have done.
texts.hos.6.10: In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing, There [is] the whoredom of Ephraim -- defiled is Israel.
texts.hos.6.11: Also, O Judah, appointed is a harvest to thee, In My turning back [to] the captivity of My people!
texts.hos.7.1: `When I give healing to Israel, Then revealed is the iniquity of Ephraim, And the wickedness of Samaria, For they have wrought falsehood, And a thief doth come in, Stript off hath a troop in the street,
texts.hos.7.2: And they do not say to their heart, [That] all their evil I have remembered, Now compassed them have their doings, Over-against My face they have been.
texts.hos.7.3: With their wickedness they make glad a king, And with their lies -- princes.
texts.hos.7.4: All of them [are] adulterers, Like a burning oven of a baker, He ceaseth from stirring up after kneading the dough, till its leavening.
texts.hos.7.5: A day of our king! Princes have polluted themselves [with] the poison of wine, He hath drawn out his hand with scorners.
texts.hos.7.6: For they have drawn near, As an oven [is] their heart, In their lying in wait all the night sleep doth their baker, Morning! he is burning as a flaming fire.
texts.hos.7.7: All of them are warm as an oven, And they have devoured their judges, All their kings have fallen, There is none calling unto Me among them.
texts.hos.7.8: Ephraim! among peoples he mixeth himself, Ephraim hath been a cake unturned.
texts.hos.7.9: Devoured have strangers his power, And he hath not known, Also old age hath sprinkled [itself] on him, And he hath not known.
texts.hos.7.10: And humbled hath been the excellency of Israel to his face, And they have not turned back unto Jehovah their God, Nor have they sought Him for all this.
texts.hos.7.11: And Ephraim is as a simple dove without heart, Egypt they called on -- [to] Asshur they have gone.
texts.hos.7.12: When they go I spread over them My net, As the fowl of the heavens I bring them down, I chastise them as their company hath heard.
texts.hos.7.13: Wo to them, for they wandered from Me, Destruction to them, for they transgressed against Me, And I -- I ransom them, and they have spoken lies against Me,
texts.hos.7.14: And have not cried unto Me with their heart, but howl on their beds, For corn and new wine they assemble themselves, They turn aside against Me.
texts.hos.7.15: And I instructed -- I strengthened their arms, And concerning Me they think evil!
texts.hos.7.16: They turn back -- not to the Most High, They have been as a deceitful bow, Fall by sword do their princes, From the insolence of their tongue, This [is] their derision in the land of Egypt!
texts.hos.8.1: `Unto thy mouth -- a trumpet, As an eagle against the house of Jehovah, Because they transgressed My covenant, And against My law they have rebelled.
texts.hos.8.2: To Me they cry, `My God, we -- Israel -- have known Thee.'
texts.hos.8.3: Cast off good hath Israel, an enemy pursueth him.
texts.hos.8.4: They have made kings, and not by Me, They have made princes, and I have not known, Their silver and their gold they have made to them idols, So that they are cut off.
texts.hos.8.5: Cast off hath thy calf, O Samaria, Burned hath Mine anger against them, Till when are they not capable of purity?
texts.hos.8.6: For even it [is] of Israel; an artificer made it, And it [is] not God, For the calf of Samaria is fragments!
texts.hos.8.7: For wind they sow, and a hurricane they reap, Stalk it hath none -- a shoot not yielding grain, If so be it yield -- strangers do swallow it up.
texts.hos.8.8: Israel hath been swallowed up, Now they have been among nations, As a vessel in which is no delight.
texts.hos.8.9: For they -- they have gone up [to] Asshur, A wild ass alone by himself [is] Ephraim, They have hired lovers!
texts.hos.8.10: Also though they hire among nations, Now I gather them, and they are pained a little, From the burden of a king of princes.
texts.hos.8.11: Because Ephraim did multiply altars to sin, They have been to him altars to sin.
texts.hos.8.12: I write for him numerous things of My law, As a strange thing they have been reckoned.
texts.hos.8.13: The sacrifices of Mine offerings! They sacrifice flesh, and they eat, Jehovah hath not accepted them, Now doth He remember their iniquity, And inspect their sin, They -- [to] Egypt they turn back.
texts.hos.8.14: And forget doth Israel his Maker, and buildeth temples, And Judah hath multiplied cities of defence, And I have sent a fire into his cities, And it hath consumed their palaces!
texts.hos.9.1: `Rejoice not, O Israel, be not joyful like the peoples, For thou hast gone a-whoring from thy God, Thou hast loved a gift near all floors of corn.
texts.hos.9.2: Floor and wine-press do not delight them, And new wine doth fail in her,
texts.hos.9.3: They do not abide in the land of Jehovah, And turned back hath Ephraim [to] Egypt, And in Asshur an unclean thing they eat.
texts.hos.9.4: They pour not out wine to Jehovah, Nor are they sweet to Him, Their sacrifices [are] as bread of mourners to them, All eating it are unclean: For their bread [is] for themselves, It doth not come into the house of Jehovah.
texts.hos.9.5: What do ye at the day appointed? And at the day of Jehovah's festival?
texts.hos.9.6: For, lo, they have gone because of destruction, Egypt gathereth them, Moph burieth them, The desirable things of their silver, Nettles possess them -- a thorn [is] in their tents.
texts.hos.9.7: Come in have the days of inspection, Come in have the days of recompence, Israel doth know! a fool [is] the prophet, Mad [is] the man of the Spirit, Because of the abundance of thine iniquity, And great [is] the hatred.
texts.hos.9.8: Ephraim is looking [away] from My God, The prophet! a snare of a fowler [is] over all his ways, Hatred [is] in the house of his God.
texts.hos.9.9: They have gone deep -- have done corruptly, As [in] the days of Gibeah, He doth remember their iniquity, He doth inspect their sins.
texts.hos.9.10: As grapes in a wilderness I found Israel, As the first-fruit in a fig-tree, at its beginning, I have seen your fathers, They -- they have gone in [to] Baal-Peor, And are separated to a shameful thing, And are become abominable like their love.
texts.hos.9.11: Ephraim [is] as a fowl, Fly away doth their honour, without birth, And without womb, and without conception.
texts.hos.9.12: For though they nourish their sons, I have made them childless -- without man, Surely also, wo to them, when I turn aside from them.
texts.hos.9.13: Ephraim! when I have looked to the rock, Is planted in comeliness, And Ephraim [is] to bring out unto a slayer his sons.
texts.hos.9.14: Give to them, Jehovah -- what dost Thou give? Give to them miscarrying womb, and dry breasts.
texts.hos.9.15: All their evil [is] in Gilgal, Surely there I have hated them, Because of the evil of their doings, Out of My house I do drive them, I add not to love them, all their heads [are] apostates.
texts.hos.9.16: Ephraim hath been smitten, Their root hath dried up, fruit they yield not, Yea, though they bring forth, I have put to death the desired of their womb.
texts.hos.9.17: Reject them doth my God, Because they have not hearkened to Him, And they are wanderers among nations!
texts.hos.10.1: `An empty vine [is] Israel, Fruit he maketh like to himself, According to the abundance of his fruit, He hath multiplied for the altars, According to the goodness of his land, They have made goodly standing-pillars.
texts.hos.10.2: Their heart hath been divided, now they are guilty, He doth break down their altars, He doth destroy their standing-pillars.
texts.hos.10.3: For now they say: We have no king, Because we have not feared Jehovah, And the king -- what doth he for us?
texts.hos.10.4: They have spoken words, To swear falsehood in making a covenant, And flourished as a poisonous herb hath judgment, on the furrows of a field.
texts.hos.10.5: For the calves of Beth-Aven fear do inhabitants of Samaria, Surely mourned on account of it hath its people, And its priests on account of it leap about, Because of its honour, for it hath removed from it,
texts.hos.10.6: Also it to Asshur is carried, a present to a warlike king, Shame doth Ephraim receive, And ashamed is Israel of its own counsel.
texts.hos.10.7: Cut off is Samaria! Its king [is] as a chip on the face of the waters.
texts.hos.10.8: And destroyed have been high places of Aven, the sin of Israel. Thorn and bramble go up on their altars, And they have said to hills, Cover us, And to heights, Fall upon us.
texts.hos.10.9: From the days of Gibeah thou hast sinned, O Israel, There they have stood, Not overtake them in Gibeah doth battle, Because of sons of perverseness.
texts.hos.10.10: When I desire, then I do bind them, And gathered against them have peoples, When they bind themselves to their two iniquities.
texts.hos.10.11: And Ephraim [is] a trained heifer -- loving to thresh, And I -- I have passed over on the goodness of its neck, I cause [one] to ride Ephraim, Plough doth Judah, harrow for him doth Jacob.
texts.hos.10.12: Sow for yourselves in righteousness, Reap according to loving-kindness, Till for yourselves tillage of knowledge, To seek Jehovah, Till he come and shew righteousness to you.
texts.hos.10.13: Ye have ploughed wickedness, Perversity ye have reaped, Ye have eaten the fruit of lying, For thou hast trusted in thy way, In the abundance of thy might.
texts.hos.10.14: And rise doth a tumult among thy people, And all thy fortresses are spoiled, As the spoiling of Shalman of Beth-Arbel, In a day of battle, Mother against sons dashed in pieces.
texts.hos.10.15: Thus hath Beth-El done to you, Because of the evil of your wickedness, In the dawn cut off utterly is a king of Israel!
texts.hos.11.1: Because Israel [is] a youth, and I love him, Out of Egypt I have called for My Son.
texts.hos.11.2: They have called to them rightly, They have gone from before them, To lords they do sacrifice, And to graven images they make perfume.
texts.hos.11.3: And I have caused Ephraim to go on foot, Taking them by their arms, And they have not known that I strengthened them.
texts.hos.11.4: With cords of man I do draw them, With thick cords of love, And I am to them as a raiser up of a yoke on their jaws, And I incline unto him -- I feed [him].
texts.hos.11.5: He turneth not back unto the land of Egypt, And Asshur -- he [is] his king, For they have refused to return.
texts.hos.11.6: Grievous hath been the sword in his cities, And it hath ended his bars, and consumed -- from their own counsels.
texts.hos.11.7: And My people are hanging in suspense, about My returning, And unto the Most High they do call, Together they exalt not.
texts.hos.11.8: How do I give thee up, O Ephraim? Do I deliver thee up, O Israel? How do I make thee as Admah? Do I set thee as Zeboim? Turned in Me is My heart, kindled together have been My repentings.
texts.hos.11.9: I do not the fierceness of My anger, I turn not back to destroy Ephraim, For God I [am], and not a man. In thy midst the Holy One, and I enter not in enmity,
texts.hos.11.10: After Jehovah they go -- as a lion He roareth, When He doth roar, then tremble do the sons from the west.
texts.hos.11.11: They tremble as a sparrow out of Egypt, And as a dove out of the land of Asshur, And I have caused them to dwell in their own houses, An affirmation of Jehovah.
texts.hos.11.12: Compassed Me with feigning hath Ephraim, And with deceit the house of Israel. And Judah again is ruling with God, And with the Holy Ones [is] faithful!
texts.hos.12.1: Ephraim is enjoying wind, And is pursuing an east wind, All the day lying and spoiling he multiplieth, And a covenant with Asshur they make, And oil to Egypt is carried.
texts.hos.12.2: And a controversy hath Jehovah with Judah, To lay a charge on Jacob according to his ways, According to his doings He returneth to him.
texts.hos.12.3: In the womb he took his brother by the heel, And by his strength he was a prince with God,
texts.hos.12.4: Yea, he is a prince unto the Messenger, And he overcometh [by] weeping, And he maketh supplication to Him, At Bethel He doth find him, And there He doth speak with us,
texts.hos.12.5: Even Jehovah, God of the Hosts, Jehovah [is] His memorial.
texts.hos.12.6: And thou, through thy God, dost turn, Kindness and judgment keep thou, And wait on thy God continually.
texts.hos.12.7: Canaan! in his hand [are] balances of deceit! To oppress he hath loved.
texts.hos.12.8: And Ephraim saith: `Surely I have become rich, I have found wealth for myself, All my labours -- they find not against me iniquity that [is] sin.'
texts.hos.12.9: And I -- Jehovah thy God from the land of Egypt, Again do I turn thee back into tents, As in the days of the appointed time.
texts.hos.12.10: And I have spoken unto the prophets, And I have multiplied vision, And by the hand of the prophets I use similes.
texts.hos.12.11: Surely Gilead [is] iniquity, Only, vanity they have been, In Gilead bullocks they have sacrificed, Also their altars [are] as heaps, on the furrows of a field.
texts.hos.12.12: And Jacob doth flee to the country of Aram, And Israel doth serve for a wife, Yea, for a wife he hath kept watch.
texts.hos.12.13: And by a prophet hath Jehovah brought up Israel out of Egypt, And by a prophet it hath been watched.
texts.hos.12.14: Ephraim hath provoked most bitterly, And his blood on himself he leaveth, And his reproach turn back to him doth his Lord!
texts.hos.13.1: When Ephraim speaketh tremblingly, He hath been lifted up in Israel, When he becometh guilty in Baal he dieth.
texts.hos.13.2: And now do they add to sin, And make to them a molten image of their silver, By their own understanding -- idols, A work of artizans -- all of it, Of them they say, who [are] sacrificers among men, `The calves let them kiss.'
texts.hos.13.3: Therefore they are as a cloud of the morning, And as dew, rising early, going away, As chaff tossed about out of a floor, And as smoke out of a window.
texts.hos.13.4: And I [am] Jehovah thy God from the land of Egypt, And a God besides Me thou dost not know, And a Saviour -- there is none save Me.
texts.hos.13.5: I -- I have known thee in a wilderness, In a land of droughts.
texts.hos.13.6: According to their feedings they are satiated, They have been satiated, And their heart is lifted up, Therefore they have forgotten Me,
texts.hos.13.7: And I am to them as a lion, As a leopard by the way I look out.
texts.hos.13.8: I do meet them as a bereaved bear, And I rend the enclosure of their heart.
texts.hos.13.9: And I consume them there as a lioness, A beast of the field doth rend them.
texts.hos.13.10: Thou hast destroyed thyself, O Israel, But in Me [is] thy help, Where [is] thy king now -- And he doth save thee in all thy cities? And thy judges of whom thou didst say, `Give to me a king and heads?'
texts.hos.13.11: I give to thee a king in Mine anger, And I take away in My wrath.
texts.hos.13.12: Bound up [is] the iniquity of Ephraim, Hidden [is] his sin,
texts.hos.13.13: Pangs of a travailing woman come to him, He [is] a son not wise, For he remaineth not the time for the breaking forth of sons.
texts.hos.13.14: From the hand of Sheol I do ransom them, From death I redeem them, Where [is] thy plague, O death? Where thy destruction, O Sheol? Repentance is hid from Mine eyes.
texts.hos.13.15: Though he among brethren produceth fruit, Come in doth an east wind, a wind of Jehovah, From a wilderness it is coming up, And it drieth up his fountain, And become dry doth his spring, It -- it spoileth a treasure -- every desirable vessel.
texts.hos.13.16: Become desolate doth Samaria, Because she hath rebelled against her God, By sword they do fall, Their sucklings are dashed in pieces, And its pregnant ones are ripped up!
texts.hos.14.1: Turn back, O Israel, unto Jehovah thy God, For thou hast stumbled by thine iniquity.
texts.hos.14.2: Take with you words, and turn to Jehovah, Say ye unto Him: `Take away all iniquity, and give good, And we do render the fruit of our lips.
texts.hos.14.3: Asshur doth not save us, on a horse we ride not, Nor do we say any more, Our God, to the work of our hands, For in Thee find mercy doth the fatherless.'
texts.hos.14.4: I heal their backsliding, I love them freely, For turned back hath Mine anger from him.
texts.hos.14.5: I am as dew to Israel, he flourisheth as a lily, And he striketh forth his roots as Lebanon.
texts.hos.14.6: Go on do his sucklings, And his beauty is as an olive, And he hath fragrance as Lebanon.
texts.hos.14.7: Return do the dwellers under his shadow, They revive [as] corn, and flourish as a vine, His memorial [is] as wine of Lebanon.
texts.hos.14.8: O Ephraim, what to Me any more with idols? I -- I afflicted, and I cause him to sing: `I [am] as a green fir-tree,' From Me is thy fruit found.
texts.hos.14.9: Who [is] wise, and doth understand these? Prudent, and knoweth them? For upright are the ways of Jehovah, And the righteous go on in them, And the transgressors stumble therein!

texts.hos.1.1: Palabra de Jehová que fue a Oséas, hijo de Beerí, en días de Ozías, Joatán, Acaz, Ezequías, reyes de Judá; y en días de Jeroboam, hijo de Joas, rey de Israel.
texts.hos.1.2: El principio de la palabra de Jehová con Oséas. Y dijo Jehová a Oséas: Vé, tómate una mujer fornicaria, e hijos de fornicaciones; porque la tierra fornicará fornicando de en pos de Jehová.
texts.hos.1.3: Y fue, y tomó a Gomer, hija de Diblaim, la cual concibió, y le parió un hijo.
texts.hos.1.4: Y díjole Jehová: Pónle por nombre Jezrael; porque de aquí a poco yo visitaré las sangres de Jezrael sobre la casa de Jehú, y haré cesar el reino de la casa de Israel.
texts.hos.1.5: Y acaecerá que en aquel día yo quebraré el arco de Israel en el valle de Jezrael.
texts.hos.1.6: Y concibió aun, y parió una hija; y díjole: Pónle por nombre Lo-ruhama; porque nunca más tendré misericordia de la casa de Israel, mas del todo los quitaré.
texts.hos.1.7: Y de la casa de Judá tendré misericordia, y salvarlos he en Jehová su Dios; y no los salvaré con arco, ni con espada, ni con batalla, ni con caballos, ni caballeros.
texts.hos.1.8: Y después de haber destetado a Lo-ruhama, concibió, y parió un hijo.
texts.hos.1.9: Y dijo: Pónle por nombre Lo-ammi; porque vosotros no sois mi pueblo, ni yo seré vuestro.
texts.hos.1.10: ¶ Y será el número de los hijos de Israel como la arena de la mar, que ni se puede medir ni contar. Y será que donde se les decía: Vosotros no sois mi pueblo; les sea dicho: Hijos del Dios viviente.
texts.hos.1.11: Y los hijos de Judá y de Israel serán congregados en uno, y levantarán para sí una cabeza, y subirán de la tierra; porque el día de Jezrael es grande.
texts.hos.2.1: Decíd a vuestros hermanos: Ammi; y a vuestras hermanas: Ruhama.
texts.hos.2.2: Pleitéad con vuestra madre, pleitéad; porque ella no es mi mujer, ni yo su marido; y quite sus fornicaciones de su rostro, y sus adulterios de entre sus pechos:
texts.hos.2.3: Porque yo no la despoje desnuda, y la haga tornar como el día en que nació, y la ponga como un desierto, y la ponga como tierra seca, y la mate de sed.
texts.hos.2.4: Ni tendré misericordia de sus hijos; porque son hijos de fornicaciones.
texts.hos.2.5: Porque su madre fornicó: avergonzóse la que los engendró, porque dijo: Iré tras mis enamorados, que me dan mi pan y mi agua, mi lana y mi lino, mi aceite y mi bebida.
texts.hos.2.6: Por tanto he aquí que yo cerco tu camino con espinas, y cercaré con seto, y no hallará sus caminos.
texts.hos.2.7: Y seguirá sus enamorados, y no los alcanzará: buscarlos ha, y no los hallará: entonces dirá: Iré, y volverme he a mi primer marido; porque mejor me iba entonces que ahora.
texts.hos.2.8: Y ella no sabía que yo le daba el trigo, y el vino, y el aceite; y les multipliqué la plata y el oro con que hicieron a Baal.
texts.hos.2.9: Por tanto yo tornaré, y tomaré mi trigo a su tiempo, y mi vino a su sazón, y quitaré mi lana y mi lino, que había dado para cubrir su desnudez.
texts.hos.2.10: Y ahora yo descubriré su vileza delante de los ojos de sus enamorados, y nadie la escapará de mi mano.
texts.hos.2.11: Y haré cesar todo su gozo, su fiesta, su nueva luna, y su sábado, y todas sus festividades.
texts.hos.2.12: Y haré talar su vid y su higuera, de que ha dicho: Mi salario me son, que me han dado mis enamorados. Y ponerlas he por monte, y comerlas han las bestias del campo.
texts.hos.2.13: Y visitaré sobre ella los tiempos de los Baales, a los cuales incensaba, y adornábase de sus zarcillos y de sus joyeles, y se iba tras sus enamorados, olvidada de mí, dice Jehová.
texts.hos.2.14: ¶ Por tanto he aquí que yo la induciré, y la llevaré al desierto, y hablaré a su corazón.
texts.hos.2.15: Y darle he sus viñas desde allí, y el valle de Acor en puerta de esperanza; y allí cantará como en los tiempos de su juventud, y como en el día de su subida de la tierra de Egipto.
texts.hos.2.16: Y será que en aquel tiempo, dice Jehová, me llamarás: Marido mío; y nunca más me llamarás: Baalí.
texts.hos.2.17: Porque quitaré de su boca los nombres de los Baales, y nunca más serán mentados por su nombre.
texts.hos.2.18: Y haré por ellos concierto en aquel tiempo con las bestias del campo, y con las aves del cielo, y con las serpientes de la tierra; y quebraré arco, y espada, y batalla de la tierra, y hacerlos he dormir seguros.
texts.hos.2.19: Y desposarte he conmigo para siempre; desposarte he conmigo en justicia, y juicio, y misericordia, y miseraciones.
texts.hos.2.20: Y desposarte he conmigo en fe, y conocerás a Jehová.
texts.hos.2.21: Y será que en aquel tiempo yo responderé, dice Jehová, yo responderé a los cielos, y ellos responderán a la tierra.
texts.hos.2.22: Y la tierra responderá al trigo, y al vino, y al aceite; y ellos responderán a Jezrael.
texts.hos.2.23: Y sembrarla he para mí en la tierra, y habré misericordia de Lo-ruhama; y diré a Lo-ammi: Pueblo mío tú; y él dirá: Dios mío.
texts.hos.3.1: Y díjome Jehová: Vé aun otra vez, y ama una mujer amada de su compañero, y adúltera, como el amor de Jehová con los hijos de Israel, los cuales miran a dioses ajenos, y aman frascos de vino.
texts.hos.3.2: Y la compré para mí por quince dineros de plata, y un homer y medio de cebada.
texts.hos.3.3: Y díjele: Tú estarás por mía muchos días: no fornicarás, ni tomarás otro varón; ni tampoco yo vendré a ti.
texts.hos.3.4: Porque muchos días estarán los hijos de Israel sin rey, y sin señor, y sin sacrificio, y sin estatua, y sin efod, y sin terafim.
texts.hos.3.5: ¶ Después volverán los hijos de Israel, y buscarán a Jehová su Dios, y a David su rey; y temerán a Jehová, y a su bondad en el fin de los días.
texts.hos.4.1: Oíd palabra de Jehová, hijos de Israel; porque Jehová pleitea con los moradores de la tierra; porque no hay verdad, ni misericordia, ni conocimiento de Dios en la tierra.
texts.hos.4.2: Perjurar, y mentir, y matar, y hurtar, y adulterar prevalecieron, y sangres se tocaron contra sangres.
texts.hos.4.3: Por lo cual la tierra se enlutará, y será talado todo morador de ella, con las bestias del campo, y las aves del cielo; y aun los peces de la mar serán cogidos.
texts.hos.4.4: Ciertamente hombre no contienda ni reprenda a hombre; porque tu pueblo es como los que resisten al sacerdote.
texts.hos.4.5: Caerás pues en este día, y caerá también contigo el profeta de noche; y a tu madre talaré.
texts.hos.4.6: Mi pueblo fue talado, porque le faltó sabiduría. Porque tú desechaste la sabiduría, yo te echaré del sacerdocio; y pues que olvidaste la ley de tu Dios, también yo me olvidaré de tus hijos.
texts.hos.4.7: Conforme a su grandeza así pecaron contra mí: yo pues también trocaré su honra en vergüenza.
texts.hos.4.8: Comen del pecado de mi pueblo, y en su maldad levantan su alma.
texts.hos.4.9: Y tal será el pueblo como el sacerdote; y visitaré sobre él sus caminos, y pagarle he conforme a sus obras.
texts.hos.4.10: Y comerán, mas no se hartarán: fornicarán, mas no se aumentarán, porque dejaron de guardar a Jehová.
texts.hos.4.11: Fornicación, y vino, y mosto quitan el corazón.
texts.hos.4.12: Mi pueblo en su madera pregunta, y su palo le responde; porque espíritu de fornicaciones le engañó, y fornicaron debajo de sus dioses.
texts.hos.4.13: Sobre los cabezos de los montes sacrificaron, y sobre los collados incensaron: debajo de encinas, y álamos, y olmos que tuviesen buena sombra: por tanto vuestras hijas fornicarán, y vuestras nueras adulterarán.
texts.hos.4.14: No visitaré sobre vuestras hijas cuando fornicaren, ni sobre vuestras nueras cuando adulteraren; porque ellos ofrecen con las rameras, y con las malas mujeres sacrifican: por tanto el pueblo sin entendimiento caerá.
texts.hos.4.15: Si fornicares tú, Israel, a lo menos no peque Judá; y no entréis en Gálgala, ni subáis a Bet-aven, ni juréis: Vive Jehová.
texts.hos.4.16: Porque como becerra cerrera revacó Israel: apaciéntalos ahora Jehová, como a carneros en anchura.
texts.hos.4.17: Efraím es dado a ídolos, déjale.
texts.hos.4.18: Su bebida se corrompió, fornicando fornicaron, amaron los dones: lo cual es afrenta de sus príncipes.
texts.hos.4.19: Atóla el viento en sus alas, y de sus sacrificios serán avergonzados.
texts.hos.5.1: Sacerdotes, oíd esto, y estád atentos, casa de Israel, y casa del rey, escuchád; porque a vosotros es el juicio; porque habéis sido lazo en Maspad, y red extendida sobre Tabor.
texts.hos.5.2: Y matando sacrificios han bajado hasta el profundo, y yo la corrección de todos ellos.
texts.hos.5.3: ¶ Yo conozco a Efraím, e Israel no me es ignorado; porque ahora has fornicado, o! Efraím, y se ha contaminado Israel.
texts.hos.5.4: No pondrán sus pensamientos en volverse a su Dios, porque espíritu de fornicación está en medio de ellos, y no conocen a Jehová.
texts.hos.5.5: Y la soberbia de Israel le desmentirá en su cara; e Israel y Efraím tropezarán en su pecado, tropezará también con ellos Judá.
texts.hos.5.6: Con sus ovejas, y con sus vacas andarán buscando a Jehová, y no le hallarán: apartóse de ellos.
texts.hos.5.7: Contra Jehová se rebelaron, porque engendraron hijos extraños: ahora los devorará mes con sus heredades.
texts.hos.5.8: Tocád bocina en Gabaa, trompeta en Rama: sonád atambor en Bet-aven, tras ti, o! Ben-jamín.
texts.hos.5.9: Efraím será asolado el día del castigo: en las tribus de Israel hice conocer mi verdad.
texts.hos.5.10: Los príncipes de Judá fueron como los que traspasan mojones: derramaré pues sobre ellos, como agua, mi ira.
texts.hos.5.11: Calumniado Efraím, quebrantado en juicio, porque quiso andar tras mandamientos.
texts.hos.5.12: Y yo seré como polilla a Efraím, y como carcoma a la casa de Judá.
texts.hos.5.13: Y verá Efraím su enfermedad, y Judá su llaga; e irá Efraím al Asur, y enviará al rey de Jareb: mas él no os podrá sanar, ni os curará la llaga.
texts.hos.5.14: Porque yo seré como león a Efraím, y como cachorro de león a la casa de Judá: yo, yo arrebataré, y andaré: tomaré, y no habrá quien escape.
texts.hos.5.15: Andaré, y tornaré a mi lugar, hasta que conozcan su pecado, y busquen mi faz: en su angustia madruguen a mí.
texts.hos.6.1: Veníd, y tornémosnos a Jehová, que él arrebató, y curarnos ha: hirió, y vendarnos ha.
texts.hos.6.2: Darnos ha vida después de dos días: al tercero día nos resucitará, y viviremos delante de él.
texts.hos.6.3: Y conoceremos: proseguiremos en conocer a Jehová: como el alba, está aparejada su salida, y vendrán a nosotros como la lluvia: como la lluvia tardía y temprana a la tierra.
texts.hos.6.4: ¿Qué haré a ti, Efraím? ¿Qué haré a ti, Judá? Vuestra misericordia, como la nube de la mañana, y como el rocío que viene a la madrugada.
texts.hos.6.5: Por esta causa corté con los profetas, con las palabras de mi boca los maté; porque tus juicios fuesen como luz que sale.
texts.hos.6.6: Porque misericordia quise, y no sacrificio; y conocimiento de Dios, mas que holocaustos.
texts.hos.6.7: ¶ Y ellos transpasaron el concierto como de hombre: allí se rebelaron contra mí.
texts.hos.6.8: Galaad, ciudad de obradores de iniquidad, ensuciada de sangre.
texts.hos.6.9: Y como ladrones que esperan a algún varón, cuadrilla de sacerdotes de común acuerdo mata en el camino; porque ponen en efecto la abominación.
texts.hos.6.10: En la casa de Israel ví suciedad: allí fornicó Efraím, se contaminó Israel.
texts.hos.6.11: También Judá puso en ti una planta, habiendo yo vuelto la cautividad de mi pueblo.
texts.hos.7.1: Estando yo curando a Israel, descubrióse la iniquidad de Efraím, y las maldades de Samaria; porque obraron engaño; y el ladrón viene: despoja el salteador de fuera.
texts.hos.7.2: Y no dicen en su corazón, que tengo en la memoria toda su maldad: ahora pues los rodearán sus obras: delante de mi presencia están.
texts.hos.7.3: Con su maldad alegran al rey, y a los príncipes con sus mentiras.
texts.hos.7.4: Todos ellos adúlteros, como horno encendido por el hornero: el cual cesará de despertar después que esté hecha la masa, hasta que esté leuda.
texts.hos.7.5: El día de nuestro rey los príncipes le hicieron enfermar con cuero de vino: extendió su mano con los burladores.
texts.hos.7.6: Porque aplicaron, como horno, su corazón asechando: toda la noche duerme su hornero: a la mañana está su horno encendido como llama de fuego.
texts.hos.7.7: Todos ellos hierven como un horno; y comieron a sus jueces: cayeron todos sus reyes: no hay entre ellos quien clame a mí.
texts.hos.7.8: Efraím se envolvió con los pueblos: Efraím fue torta no vuelta.
texts.hos.7.9: Comieron extraños su sustancia, y él no lo supo; y aun vejez se ha esparcido por él, y él no lo entendió.
texts.hos.7.10: Y la soberbia de Israel testificará contra él en su cara; y no se tornaron a Jehová su Dios, ni le buscaron con todo esto.
texts.hos.7.11: Y fue Efraím como paloma, engañada sin entendimiento: llamarán a Egipto, irán al Asur.
texts.hos.7.12: Cuando fueren, extenderé sobre ellos mi red, hacerlos he caer como aves del cielo: castigarlos he conforme a lo que se ha oído en sus congregaciones.
texts.hos.7.13: ¡Ay de ellos! porque se apartaron de mí: destrucción sobre ellos; porque se rebelaron contra mí: yo los redemí, y ellos hablaron contra mí mentiras.
texts.hos.7.14: Y no clamaron a mí con su corazón, cuando aullaron sobre sus camas: para el trigo y el mosto se congregaron: se rebelaron contra mí.
texts.hos.7.15: Y yo los ceñí, esforcé sus brazos, y contra mí pensaron mal.
texts.hos.7.16: Tornáronse, mas no al Altísimo: fueron como arco engañoso: cayeron sus príncipes a cuchillo por la soberbia de su lengua: este será su escarnio en la tierra de Egipto.
texts.hos.8.1: Pon a tu boca trompeta, como águila, contra la casa de Jehová, porque traspasaron mi concierto, y contra mi ley se rebelaron.
texts.hos.8.2: A mí clamarán Israel: Dios mío, te conocimos.
texts.hos.8.3: Desamparó Israel el bien: enemigo le perseguirá.
texts.hos.8.4: ¶ Ellos hicieron reinar, mas no por mí: constituyeron príncipe, mas yo no lo supe: de su plata, y de su oro hicieron ídolos para sí, para ser talados.
texts.hos.8.5: Tu becerro, o! Samaria, te hizo alejar: mi enojo se encendió contra ellos, hasta que no pudieron alcanzar inocencia.
texts.hos.8.6: Porque de Israel es, y artífice lo hizo, que no es Dios; porque en pedazos será deshecho el becerro de Samaria.
texts.hos.8.7: Porque sembraron viento, y torbellino segarán: no tendrán mies, ni el fruto hará harina: si la hiciere, extraños la tragarán.
texts.hos.8.8: Será tragado Israel: presto serán tenidos entre las gentes como vaso en que no hay contentamiento.
texts.hos.8.9: Porque ellos subieron a Asur, asno montés para sí solo: Efraím con salario alquiló armadores.
texts.hos.8.10: Aunque alquilen a las naciones, ahora las juntaré; y serán un poco afligidos por la carga del rey, y de los príncipes.
texts.hos.8.11: Porque multiplicó Efraím altares para pecar, tuvo altares para pecar.
texts.hos.8.12: Escribíle las grandezas de mi ley, fueron tenidas por cosas ajenas.
texts.hos.8.13: Los sacrificios de mis dones, sacrificaron carne, y comieron, Jehová no los quiso: ahora se acordará de su iniquidad, y visitará su pecado: ellos tornarán a Egipto.
texts.hos.8.14: Olvidó pues Israel a su Hacedor, y edificó templos, y Judá multiplicó ciudades fuertes: y yo meteré fuego en sus ciudades, el cual devorará sus palacios.
texts.hos.9.1: No te alegres, o! Israel, hasta saltar de gozo como los pueblos; pues has fornicado de tu Dios: amaste salario de ramera por todas las eras de trigo.
texts.hos.9.2: La era, y el lagar no los mantendrá: el mosto les mentirá.
texts.hos.9.3: No quedarán en la tierra de Jehová: mas volverá Efraím a Egipto, y a Asiria, donde comerán vianda inmunda.
texts.hos.9.4: No derramarán vino a Jehová, ni él tomará contento en sus sacrificios: como pan de enlutados les serán a ellos; todos los que comieren de él, serán inmundos; porque su pan por su alma no entrará en la casa de Jehová.
texts.hos.9.5: ¿Qué haréis el día de la solemnidad, y el día de la fiesta de Jehová?
texts.hos.9.6: Porque he aquí que ellos se fueron después de su destrucción: Egipto los cogerá, Mémfis los enterrará, espino poseerá por heredad lo deseable de su plata, hortiga crecerá en sus moradas.
texts.hos.9.7: Vinieron los días de la visitación, vinieron los días de la paga: conocerá Israel: insensato el profeta, furioso el varón de espíritu, a causa de la multitud de tu maldad, y grande odio.
texts.hos.9.8: El atalaya de Efraím para con mi Dios, es a saber, el profeta, es lazo de cazador en todos sus caminos, odio en la casa de su Dios.
texts.hos.9.9: Llegaron al profundo, corrompiéronse, como en los días de Gabaa: ahora se acordará de su iniquidad, visitará su pecado.
texts.hos.9.10: Como uvas en el desierto hallé a Israel: como la fruta temprana de la higuera en su principio ví a vuestros padres; y ellos entraron a Baal-pehor, y se apartaron para vergüenza, e hiciéronse abominables como su amor.
texts.hos.9.11: Efraím, volará, como ave, su gloria desde el nacimiento, o, desde el vientre, o desde el concebimiento.
texts.hos.9.12: Y sí llegaren a grandes a sus hijos, yo los quitaré de entre los hombres; porque también, ¡ay de ellos, cuando de ellos me apartare!
texts.hos.9.13: Efraím, según veo, es semejante a Tiro asentada en lugar deleitoso: mas Efraím sacará sus hijos al matador.
texts.hos.9.14: Dáles, o! Jehová, lo que les has de dar: dáles matriz amovedera, y secos pechos.
texts.hos.9.15: Toda la maldad de ellos fue en Gálgala; porque allí tomé con ellos odio por la malicia de sus obras: echarlos he de mi casa: nunca más los amaré, todos sus príncipes son desleales.
texts.hos.9.16: Efraím fue herido, su cepa se secó: no hará más fruto: aunque engendren, yo mataré lo deseable de su vientre.
texts.hos.9.17: Mi Dios los desechará, porque ellos no le oyeron; y serán vagabundos entre las naciones.
texts.hos.10.1: La vid vacía a Israel, haciendo fruto para él: conforme a la multiplicación de su fruto, multiplicó altares: conforme a la bondad de su tierra, mejoraron sus estatuas.
texts.hos.10.2: Apartóse su corazón. Ahora serán convencidos: el quebrantará sus altares, asolará sus estatuas.
texts.hos.10.3: Porque ahora dirán: No tenemos rey, porque no temimos a Jehová; y el rey, ¿qué nos hará?
texts.hos.10.4: Hablaron palabras jurando en vano, haciendo alianza; y el juicio florecerá en los surcos del campo como ajenjo.
texts.hos.10.5: Por las becerras de Bet-aven serán atemorizados los moradores de Samaria; porque su pueblo lamentará por su causa; y sus sacerdotes se alegrarán a causa del, por su gloria que será perdida.
texts.hos.10.6: Y aun también será él llevado en Asiria en presente al rey de Jareb: Efraím será avergonzado, Israel será confuso de su consejo.
texts.hos.10.7: De Samaria fue cortado su rey, como la espuma sobre las haces de las aguas.
texts.hos.10.8: Y los altares de Avén serán destruidos, el pecado de Israel: crecerá sobre sus altares espino y cardo, y dirán a los montes: Cubrídnos; y a los collados: Caéd sobre nosotros.
texts.hos.10.9: Desde los días de Gabaa has pecado, o! Israel: allí estuvieron: no los tomó la batalla en Gabaa contra los inicuos.
texts.hos.10.10: Yo los castigaré como deseo; y pueblos se juntarán sobre ellos cuando serán atados en sus dos surcos.
texts.hos.10.11: Efraím, becerra domada amadora del trillar: mas yo pasaré sobre la hermosura de su pescuezo: yo haré llevar yugo a Efraím, arará Judá, quebrará sus terrones Jacob.
texts.hos.10.12: Sembrád para vosotros a justicia, segád para vosotros a misericordia, arád para vosotros arada; porque el tiempo es de buscar a Jehová hasta que venga, y os enseñe justicia.
texts.hos.10.13: Habéis arado impiedad, segasteis iniquidad, comeréis fruto de mentira; porque confiaste en tu camino, en la multitud de tus fuertes.
texts.hos.10.14: Por tanto en tus pueblos se levantará alboroto, y todas tus fortalezas serán destruidas, como en la deshecha de Salmana en Bet-arbel el día de la batalla: la madre fue arrojada sobre los hijos.
texts.hos.10.15: Así hará a vosotros Bet-el por la maldad de vuestra maldad: en la mañana cortando será cortado el rey de Israel.
texts.hos.11.1: Cuando Israel era muchacho, yo le amé, y de Egipto llamé a mi hijo.
texts.hos.11.2: Clamaban a ellos, así ellos se iban de su presencia: a los Baales sacrificaban, y a las esculturas ofrecían sahumerios.
texts.hos.11.3: Yo con todo eso guiaba en pies al mismo Efraím: levantóles en sus brazos, y no conocieron que yo los procuraba.
texts.hos.11.4: Con cuerdas humanas los traje, con cuerdas de amor; y fui para ellos como los que alzan el yugo sobre sus mejillas, y llegué hacia él la comida.
texts.hos.11.5: No tornará a tierra de Egipto, mas el mismo Asur será su rey, porque no se quisieron convertir.
texts.hos.11.6: Y caerá espada sobre sus ciudades, y consumirá sus aldeas: consumirlas ha a causa de sus consejos.
texts.hos.11.7: Mas mi pueblo está colgado de la rebelión contra mí; y aunque le llaman al Altísimo, de ninguno de todos es ensalzado.
texts.hos.11.8: ¿Cómo te dejaré, Efraím? ¿cómo te entregaré, Israel? ¿cómo te pondré como Adama, y te tornaré como Seboim? Mi corazón se revuelve dentro de mí, todos mis arrepentimientos son encendidos.
texts.hos.11.9: No ejecutaré la ira de mi furor: no me volveré para destruir a Efraím; porque Dios soy, y no hombre: Santo en medio de ti, y no entraré en ciudad.
texts.hos.11.10: En pos de Jehová caminarán: él bramará como león, él cierto bramará, y los hijos del occidente temblarán.
texts.hos.11.11: Temblarán como ave los de Egipto, y como paloma los de la tierra de Asiria; y ponerlos he en sus casas, dijo Jehová.
texts.hos.11.12: Cercóme con mentira Efraím, y con engaño la casa de Israel. Judá aun domina con Dios, y con los santos es fiel.
texts.hos.12.1: Efraím es apacentado del viento, y sigue al solano; mentira y destrucción aumenta continuamente; porque hicieron alianza con los Asirios, y aceite se lleva a Egipto.
texts.hos.12.2: Pleito tiene Jehová con Judá, para visitar a Jacob conforme a sus caminos: pagarle ha conforme a sus obras.
texts.hos.12.3: En el vientre tomó por el calcañar a su hermano; y con su fortaleza venció al ángel:
texts.hos.12.4: Y venció al ángel, y prevaleció: lloró, y rogóle: en Bet-el le halló, y allí habló con nosotros.
texts.hos.12.5: Mas Jehová es Dios de los ejércitos, Jehová es su memorial.
texts.hos.12.6: Tú pues a tu Dios te convierte, guarda misericordia y juicio, y en tu Dios espera siempre.
texts.hos.12.7: Mercader que tiene en su mano peso falso, amador de opresión.
texts.hos.12.8: Y dijo Efraím: Ciertamente yo he enriquecido: hallado he riquezas para mí: nadie hallará en mí iniquidad, ni pecado en todos mis trabajos.
texts.hos.12.9: Yo pues soy Jehová tu Dios desde la tierra de Egipto, aun te haré morar en tiendas, como en los días de la fiesta.
texts.hos.12.10: Y hablé a los profetas, y yo aumenté la profecía; y por mano de los profetas puse semejanzas.
texts.hos.12.11: ¿Galaad no es iniquidad? Ciertamente vanidad han sido: en Galaad sacrificaron bueyes; y aun sus altares como montones en los surcos del campo.
texts.hos.12.12: Y Jacob huyó en la tierra de Aram, y sirvió Israel por su mujer, y por su mujer fue pastor.
texts.hos.12.13: Y por profeta hizo subir Jehová a Israel de Egipto, y por profeta fue guardado.
texts.hos.12.14: Enojó Efraím a Dios con amarguras: por tanto sus sangres se derramarán sobre él, y su Señor le pagará su vergüenza.
texts.hos.13.1: Cuando Efraím hablaba, todos tenían temor: fue ensalzado en Israel: mas pecó en Baal, y murió.
texts.hos.13.2: Y ahora añadieron a su pecado, e hicieron para sí vaciadizo de su plata según su entendimiento: ídolos, obra de artífices todo ello, de los cuales ellos mandan a los hombres que sacrifican, que besen los becerros.
texts.hos.13.3: Por tanto serán como la niebla de la mañana, y como el rocío de la madrugada que se pasa: como el tamo que la tempestad lanza de la era, y como el humo que sale por la ventana.
texts.hos.13.4: Mas yo soy Jehová tu Dios desde la tierra de Egipto: por tanto no conocerás otro Dios fuera de mí, no otro salvador si no a mí.
texts.hos.13.5: Yo te conocí en el desierto, en tierra de sequedades.
texts.hos.13.6: En sus pastos se hartaron, hartáronse, y ensoberbecióse su corazón, por esta causa se olvidaron de mí.
texts.hos.13.7: Por tanto yo seré para ellos como león, como tigre que asecha cerca del camino.
texts.hos.13.8: Como oso que ha perdido los hijos los encontraré, y les romperé las telas de su corazón; y allí los tragaré como león: bestia del campo los despedazará.
texts.hos.13.9: Echóte a perder, o! Israel, tu idolatría: mas en mí está tu ayuda.
texts.hos.13.10: ¿En dónde está tu rey, para que te guarde con todas tus ciudades? ¿y tus jueces, de los cuales dijiste: Dáme rey, y príncipes?
texts.hos.13.11: Díte rey en mi furor, y le quité en mi ira.
texts.hos.13.12: Atada está la maldad de Efraím: su pecado está guardado.
texts.hos.13.13: Dolores de mujer de parto le vendrán: es un hijo ignorante, que de otra manera no estuviera tanto tiempo en el rompimiento de los hijos.
texts.hos.13.14: ¶ De la mano del sepulcro los redimiré, de la muerte los libraré. ¡O muerte! yo seré tu mortandad; y seré tu destrucción, ¡o sepulcro! Arrepentimiento será escondido de mis ojos.
texts.hos.13.15: Porque él fructificará entre los hermanos: vendrá el solano, viento de Jehová, subiendo de la parte del desierto, y secarse ha su vena, y secarse ha su manadero: él saqueará el tesoro de todas las alhajas de codicia.
texts.hos.13.16: Samaria será asolada porque se rebeló contra su Dios: caerán a cuchillo: sus niños serán estrellados, y sus preñadas serán abiertas.
texts.hos.14.1: ¶ Conviértete, ¡O! Israel, a Jehová tu Dios; porque por tu pecado has caído.
texts.hos.14.2: Tomád con vosotros palabras, y convertíos a Jehová, y decídle: Quita toda iniquidad, y recibe el bien; y pagaremos becerros de nuestros labios.
texts.hos.14.3: No nos librará Assur, no subiremos sobre caballo, ni nunca más diremos a la obra de nuestras manos: Dioses nuestros; porque por ti el huérfano alcanzará misericordia.
texts.hos.14.4: ¶ Yo medicinaré su rebelión, amarlos he de voluntad; porque mi furor se quitó de ellos.
texts.hos.14.5: Yo seré a Israel como rocío: el florecerá, como lirio, y extenderá sus raíces, como el Líbano.
texts.hos.14.6: Extenderse han sus ramos, y será su gloria como la de la oliva, y olerá como el Líbano.
texts.hos.14.7: Volverán los que se sentaren debajo de su sombra: serán vivificados como trigo, y florecerán como la vid: su olor, como de vino del Líbano.
texts.hos.14.8: Efraím entonces dirá: ¿Qué más tendré ya con los ídolos? Yo le oiré, y miraré: yo seré a él como la haya verde: tu fruto es hallado de mí.
texts.hos.14.9: ¿Quién es sabio para que entienda esto; y prudente para que lo sepa? Porque los caminos de Jehová son derechos, y los justos andarán por ellos: mas los rebeldes caerán en ellos.

texts.hos.1.1: The word of Yahweh which came unto Hosea son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah, kings of Judah,—and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.
texts.hos.1.2: The beginning of the word of Yahweh with Hosea, was,—that Yahweh said unto Hosea, Go take thee a woman of unchastity, and the children of unchastity, for, unchastely indeed, hath the land been going away from following Yahweh.
texts.hos.1.3: So he went and took Gomer, daughter of Diblaim,—and she conceived and bare him a son.
texts.hos.1.4: Then said Yahweh unto him, Call his name Jezreel: for, yet a little, and I will visit the bloodshed of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel.
texts.hos.1.5: And it shall come to pass, in that day, that I will break the bow of Israel, in the vale of Jezreel.
texts.hos.1.6: Then conceived she again and bare a daughter, and he said to him, Call her name Lo-ruhamah ["Uncompassionated"],—for, not again any more, will I have compassion upon the house of Israel, that I should, forgive, them;
texts.hos.1.7: but, on the house of Judah, will I have compassion, and I will save them, as Yahweh their God,—but will not save them by bow, or by sword, or by battle, by horses, or by horsemen.
texts.hos.1.8: And, when she had weaned Lo-ruhamah, she conceived, and bare a son.
texts.hos.1.9: Then said he, Call his name Lo-ammi [="No people of mine"],—for ye are Lo-ammi ["No people of mine"], and, I, will not be yours.
texts.hos.1.10: Yet shall the number of the sons of Israel become like the sand of the sea, which can neither he measured, nor numbered,—and it shall come to pass, in the place where it used to be said to them, No people of mine, are ye, it shall be said to them, Sons of a Living God!
texts.hos.1.11: Then shall the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel, gather themselves together, as one, and shall appoint them one head, and come up out of the earth,—for great shall be the day of Jezreel.
texts.hos.2.1: Say ye unto your brethren, O Ammi [="O my people"], and unto your sisters, O Ruhamah [="O compassionated one"]:
texts.hos.2.2: Contend ye with your mother, contend, for she is no wife of mine, and I am no husband of hers, Let her then put away her paramours from before her, and her partners in adultery, from her embraces:
texts.hos.2.3: Lest I strip off her under-clothing, and set her forth to view, as in the day she was born,—and make her like a wilderness, and render her like a land that is parched, and suffer her to die of thirst;
texts.hos.2.4: And, on her children, not have compassion,—because, the children of paramours, they are.
texts.hos.2.5: For their mother, hath been unchaste, and she that conceived them, hath caused shame,—for she said, Let me go after my lovers! who used to give my bread, and my water, my wool, and my flax, mine oil, and my drink.
texts.hos.2.6: Therefore, behold me! hedging up her way, with thorns,—and I will wall her in, and, her footpaths, shall she not find.
texts.hos.2.7: And, when she shall pursue her lovers, and not overtake them, and shall seek them and not find, then will she say, Let me go my way now! and return unto my first husband, for it was better with me, then, than, now!
texts.hos.2.8: But, she, owneth not, that, I, gave her—the corn, and the new wine and the oil,—silver, also increased I unto her, and gold—[which] they offered to Baal!
texts.hos.2.9: Therefore, will I again take away my corn, in the time thereof, and my new wine, in the season thereof,—and will recover my wool and my flax [given] to hide her shame.
texts.hos.2.10: Now, therefore, will I expose her unseemliness, before the eyes of her lovers,—and no, man, shall deliver her out of my hand!
texts.hos.2.11: And I will cause to cease all her mirth, her pilgrim-festival, her new moon and her sabbath,—and her every appointed meeting;
texts.hos.2.12: And will lay waste her vine and her fig- tree, as to which she hath said, A present, are they for myself, which my lovers, have given me,—and I will make of them a thicket, and the wild beasts of the field shall devour them.
texts.hos.2.13: So will I visit upon her the days of the Baals, unto whom she used to burn incense, and decked herself with her nose-ring and her jewelry, and went her way after her lovers,—whereas, me, she forgat, Declareth Yahweh.
texts.hos.2.14: Therefore, lo! I, am going to persuade her, and, though I conduct her forth into wilderness, yet will I speak unto her heart.
texts.hos.2.15: Then will I give to her her vineyards from thence, and the vale of Achor [="trouble"] for a door of hope,—and she will respond there, as in the days of her youth, and as in the day when she came up out of the land of Egypt.
texts.hos.2.16: And it shall come to pass, in that day, Declareth Yahweh, that she will call me Ishi [="My husband"], and will not call me any more, Baali [="Mine owner"].
texts.hos.2.17: So will I take away the names of the Baals, out of her mouth,—and they shall not be called to mind any more, by their name.
texts.hos.2.18: And I will solemnize to them a covenant, in that day, with the wild-beast of the field, and with the bird of the heavens, and the creeping thing of the ground,—and, bow and sword and battle, will I break in pieces out of the land, so will I cause them to lie down, in security.
texts.hos.2.19: And I will take thee unto myself, unto times age-abiding,—yea I will take thee unto myself, in righteousness and in justice, and in lovingkindness, and in abounding compassion:
texts.hos.2.20: Yea I will take thee unto myself, in faithfulness,—So shalt thou know Yahweh.
texts.hos.2.21: And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will respond, Declareth Yahweh, I will respond to the heavens,—and, they, shall respond to the earth;
texts.hos.2.22: And, the earth, shall respond to the corn, and to the new wine and to the oil,—and, they, shall respond to Jezreel [="Whom GOD scattereth," "Whom GOD soweth"].
texts.hos.2.23: So will I sow her unto me in the land, and will have compassion upon the uncompassionated one [="Lo-ruhamah"],—and will say to him who was No-people-of-mine [="Lo-ammi"], My people, thou art, and, he, shall say, My God!
texts.hos.3.1: Then said Yahweh unto me, Once more, go love a woman who loveth a friend, and is an adulteress,—according to the love of Yahweh unto the sons of Israel, though they keep turning away unto other gods, and love [idolatrous] raisin-cakes.
texts.hos.3.2: So I secured her to me, for fifteen pieces of silver,—and a homer of barley, and a half-homer of barley;
texts.hos.3.3: and I said unto her, Many days, shalt thou tarry for me, thou shalt not be unchaste, neither shalt thou become another man’s,—moreover also, I, [will tarry] for thee.
texts.hos.3.4: For, many days, shall the sons of Israel tarry, without king, and without ruler, and without sacrifice, and without pillar; and without ephod, or household gods.
texts.hos.3.5: Afterwards, shall the sons of Israel return, and seek Yahweh their God, and David their king,—and shall turn with throbbing hearts unto Yahweh and unto his goodness, in the afterpart of the days.
texts.hos.4.1: Hear the word of Yahweh, ye sons of Israel,—that, a controversy, hath Yahweh with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no faithfulness, nor lovingkindness, nor knowledge of God, in the land:
texts.hos.4.2: Cursing and lying, and killing and stealing, and committing adultery, have broken forth, and, blood-shedding, unto blood-shedding, doth extend.
texts.hos.4.3: For this cause, shall the land mourn, and everyone who dwelleth therein shall languish, with the wild beast of the field and with the bird of the heavens,—moreover also, the fishes of the sea, shall be withdrawn.
texts.hos.4.4: Howbeit let, no man, contend, nor let him rebuke another,—since, thy people, are as they who contend against a priest:
texts.hos.4.5: So shouldst thou stumble in the daytime, and even the prophet stumble with thee, in the night,—and I should destroy thine own mother.
texts.hos.4.6: My people, are destroyed, for lack of knowledge,—Because, thou, hast rejected knowledge, therefore will I reject thee from ministering as priest unto me, and, because thou hast forgotten the law of thy God, I also, will forget thy children.
texts.hos.4.7: As they were magnified, so, they sinned against me,—My glory—for what was contemptible, did they exchange.
texts.hos.4.8: The sin of my people, they do eat,—and. unto their iniquity, lift they up every man his desire.
texts.hos.4.9: So doth it come to be—like people, like priest,—therefore will I visit upon him his ways, and, his doings, will I bring back to him;
texts.hos.4.10: And they shall eat, and not be satisfied, they have encouraged unchastity, yet have not been making increase,—for unto, Yahweh, have they left off giving heed:—
texts.hos.4.11: Unchastity, and wine, and new wine, take away the heart.
texts.hos.4.12: My people, of their Wood, do ask,—Let, their Staff, then tell them,—for, the spirit of unchastity, hath led them astray, and they have unchastely departed from under their God.
texts.hos.4.13: On the headlands of the mountains, they sacrifice, and, on the hills, burn they incense, under oak and poplar and terebinth, because, pleasant, is the shade thereof: For this cause, do your daughters, become unchaste, and, your brides, commit adultery.
texts.hos.4.14: I do not bring punishment upon your daughters when they become unchaste, nor upon your brides, when they commit adultery, for, the men themselves, with unchaste women, do seclude themselves, and, with the common women of the shrine, do offer sacrifice,—and, a people who will not discern, must be ruined.
texts.hos.4.15: Though unchaste art thou, O Israel, let not Judah, become guilty, neither let them enter Gilgal, nor go up to Beth-aven, and [then] swear, By the life of Yahweh!
texts.hos.4.16: For, as a heifer that is stubborn, hath Israel, been stubborn,—Now, can Yahweh, turn them out to pasture, like a young ram in a wide place?
texts.hos.4.17: Mated with idols, is Ephraim, let him alone.
texts.hos.4.18: Their drinking-bout, having passed,—they became, unchaste, they loved wildly, a contempt, became her great men.
texts.hos.4.19: The wind hath bound her up in its wings,—that they may be ashamed, because of their sacrifices.
texts.hos.5.1: Hear ye this—O priests, and attend, O house of Israel, and ye, House of the King, give ear, for, to you, pertaineth the sentence,—for, a snare, have ye been to Mizpah, and a net spread on Tabor.
texts.hos.5.2: And, a slaughter, have apostates deeply designed,—though, I, was a rebuker to them all.
texts.hos.5.3: I, have known Ephraim, and, Israel, hath not been hidden from me,—for, now, hast thou committed unchastity, O Ephraim, Israel, hath made himself impure.
texts.hos.5.4: Their doings, will not suffer, them to return unto their God,—for, the spirit of unchastity, is within them, and, Yahweh, have they not known.
texts.hos.5.5: Therefore will the Excellency of Israel, answer, to his face,—and, Israel and Ephraim, shall stumble in their iniquity, even Judah with them, hath stumbled.
texts.hos.5.6: With their flocks and with their herds, will they go to seek Yahweh, but shall not find him; he hath withdrawn himself from them.
texts.hos.5.7: With Yahweh, have they dealt treacherously, for, to alien children, have they given birth,—now, a new moon, shall devour them, with their portions.
texts.hos.5.8: Blow ye a horn in Gibeah, a trumpet in Ramah,—sound an alarm at Beth-aven, behind thee, O Benjamin!
texts.hos.5.9: Ephraim, shall become, a desolation, in the day of rebuke: Throughout the tribes of Israel, have I hide known what is sure.
texts.hos.5.10: The rulers of Judah have become as they who remove a land-mark. Upon them, will I pour out, like water, my wrath.
texts.hos.5.11: Oppressed, is Ephraim, crushed in judgment,—because he hath, wilfully, walked after falsehood.
texts.hos.5.12: But, I, was like a moth, to Ephraim,—and like rotten wood to the house of Judah.
texts.hos.5.13: When Ephraim, saw, his injury, and Judah his wound, then went Ephraim unto Assyria, and [Judah] sent unto a hostile king,—yet, he, cannot heal you, nor will the wound, remove from you.
texts.hos.5.14: For, I, will be as a lion unto Ephraim, and as a young lion to the house of Judah,—I, I, will tear in pieces, and depart, I will carry off, and none be able to rescue.
texts.hos.5.15: I will depart, will return unto my place! till what time they acknowledge their guilt, and seek my face,—In their trouble, will they make for me diligent search.
texts.hos.6.1: Come, and let us return unto Yahweh! for, he, hath torn, that he might heal us,—smitten, that he might bind us up.
texts.hos.6.2: He will bring us to life, after two days,—on the third day, will he raise us up, that we may live before him.
texts.hos.6.3: Then let us know—let us press on to know—Yahweh, Like the dawn, is his coming forth assured,—that he may come like a down-pour upon us, like the harvest-rain, [and] the seed-rain of the land.
texts.hos.6.4: What can I do unto thee, O Ephraim? What can I do unto thee, O Judah? for, your lovingkindness, is like a morning cloud, yea, like the dew, early departing!
texts.hos.6.5: For this cause, have I hewn them in pieces by the prophets, I have slain them by the sayings of my mouth,—and, my justice, as a light goeth forth.
texts.hos.6.6: For, lovingkindness, I desired, and not sacrifice,—and the knowledge of God, more than ascending-offerings.
texts.hos.6.7: But, they, like Adam, have transgressed a covenant,—There, have they dealt treacherously with me.
texts.hos.6.8: Gilead, is a city of workers of iniquity,—tracked with blood.
texts.hos.6.9: And, like liers in wait for a man, in troops, is a band of priests, on the road, will they murder towards Shechem,—because, a shameful deed, they have done.
texts.hos.6.10: In the house of Israel, have I seen a horrible thing,—there, the unchastity of Ephraim, defiled is Israel.
texts.hos.6.11: Judah too! a harvest is appointed for thee,—in that I will bring back the captivity of my people.
texts.hos.7.1: When I would have brought healing to Israel, then was disclosed the iniquity of Ephraim, and the wicked doings of Samaria, for they have wrought falsehood,—when, a thief, would enter, a band roamed about, outside,
texts.hos.7.2: And they say not to their own hearts, that, all their wickedness, I remember, now, have their doings, beset them about, right before my face, have they been done.
texts.hos.7.3: By their wickedness, they gladden a king, and, by their flatteries,—rulers.
texts.hos.7.4: They all, are adulterers, like an oven too hot for the baker,—who leaveth off stoking, after kneading the dough, till the whole be leavened.
texts.hos.7.5: In the day of our king, the rulers, have made themselves ill, with the heat of wine,—he hath extended his hand with scoffers.
texts.hos.7.6: For they have made ready, like an oven, their heart, by their lying in wait,—all the night, their baker sleepeth, in the morning, he, kindleth up as it were a blazing fire.
texts.hos.7.7: They all, become hot as an oven, and devour their judges,—all their kings, have fallen, there hath been none among them crying unto me.
texts.hos.7.8: As for Ephraim! with the peoples, hath he been mingling himself,—Ephraim, is a cake not turned.
texts.hos.7.9: Foreigners have, eaten up, his strength, and, he, knoweth it not,—even gray hairs, are sprinkled upon him, and, he, knoweth it not.
texts.hos.7.10: Therefore doth the Excellency of Israel, answer, to his face; yet have they not returned unto Yahweh their God, nor have they sought him, in spite of all this!
texts.hos.7.11: So then, Ephraim, hath become, like a simple dove, having no understanding, on Egypt, have they called, to Assyria, have they gone,
texts.hos.7.12: Whithersoever they go, I will spread over them my net, like a bird of the heavens, will I bring them down, I will chastise them, by the time the report can reach the flock of them.
texts.hos.7.13: Woe to them! for they have taken flight from me, destruction to them! for they have transgressed against me,—when, I, would have ransomed them, then, they, spake—concerning me—falsehoods.
texts.hos.7.14: Neither made they outcry unto me, in their heart, although they kept on howling upon their beds, over corn and new wine, they gathered themselves together, they rebelled against me.
texts.hos.7.15: When, I, had warned them, I strengthened their arm,—yet, against me, kept they on devising wickedness.
texts.hos.7.16: They would return—not to him who is on high! They have become like a deceitful bow, their rulers, shall fall by the sword, for the rage of their tongue, this, [shall be] their derision in the land of Egypt.
texts.hos.8.1: To thy mouth, with a horn! Like an eagle, on the house of Yahweh,—because they have violated my covenant, and, against my law, have they transgressed.
texts.hos.8.2: Unto me, shall they make outcry, My God! we acknowledge thee—[we], Israel!
texts.hos.8.3: Israel hath cast away what is good,—an enemy, shall pursue him.
texts.hos.8.4: They, have appointed kings, but not from me, have made rulers, but I have not acknowledged them: of their silver and their gold, they made themselves idols, to the end they might be cut off.
texts.hos.8.5: He hath cast away thy calf, O Samaria, kindled is mine anger upon them,—How long shall they not endure to be innocent?
texts.hos.8.6: For, of Israel, is even that thing! A craftsman, made it, and, a No-god, it is! For, into fragments, shall the Calf of Samaria be broken.
texts.hos.8.7: For, to the wind, they sow, and, to the whirlwind, they reap: stalk, hath it none, That which shooteth forth, shall yield no meal, If so be it yield, foreigners, swallow it lip,
texts.hos.8.8: Swallowed up, is Israel; Now, have they gone among the nations, like a vessel in which no man taketh, delight.
texts.hos.8.9: For, they, have gone up to Assyria, A wild ass going alone for himself, is Ephraim! They have hired lovers!
texts.hos.8.10: Even though they hire them among the nations, at once, will I gather them, when they have begun to be diminished by reason of the burden of the king of rulers.
texts.hos.8.11: Because Ephraim hath multiplied altars sinfully, they have become to him the altars of sin.
texts.hos.8.12: I have been wont to write for him the myriad things of my law,—Like something alien, have they been accounted.
texts.hos.8.13: My sacrificial gifts, have they been sacrificing as [common] flesh, and have eaten, Yahweh, hath not accepted them,—Now, will he call to mind their iniquity, that he may punish their sin, they, to Egypt, will return.
texts.hos.8.14: And so Israel hath forgotten his Maker, and hath built temples, and, Judah, hath multiplied fortified cities,—Therefore will I send a fire upon his cities, and it shall consume the palaces thereof.
texts.hos.9.1: Do not rejoice, O Israel, with exultation, like the peoples, for thou hast gone away unchastely from beside thy God,—thou hast loved a present, upon all the threshing-floors of corn!
texts.hos.9.2: Threshing-floor and wine-vat, will not feed them, and, new wine, will deny them.
texts.hos.9.3: They shall not dwell in the land of Yahweh, but Ephraim shall return to Egypt, and, in Assyria—that which is unclean, shall they eat.
texts.hos.9.4: They shall not pour out to Yahweh—wine, neither shall they be pleasing to him, their sacrifices, are as the food of mourning to them, all that eat thereof, shall defile themselves, because, their food for their appetite, entereth not into the house of Yahweh.
texts.hos.9.5: What will ye do, for the day of appointed meeting? and in the day of the festival of Yahweh?
texts.hos.9.6: For, though they have gone from destruction, yet, Egypt, shall gather them, Memphis, shall bury them,—as for their silver favorites! thistles, shall possess them, thorns in their tents.
texts.hos.9.7: Come are the days of visitation, come are the days of recompense, Let Israel know! The prophet is foolish, the man of the spirit doth rave, because of the greatness of thine iniquity, therefore great is the prosecution.
texts.hos.9.8: The watchman of Ephraim, [should have been] with my God: As for the prophet, the snare of the fowler, is on all his ways, a prosecution [awaiteth him], in the house of his God.
texts.hos.9.9: They have deeply corrupted themselves, like the days of Gibeah: he will call to mind their iniquity, he will punish their sins.
texts.hos.9.10: Like grapes in the desert, found I Israel, like the first-ripe in the fig-tree when it is young, saw I your fathers,—they, entered Baal-peor, and devoted themselves to the Shameful Thing, Then became their abominations like their lusts.
texts.hos.9.11: As for Ephraim! like a bird, did their glory, fly away,—no birth, and none with child, no conception.
texts.hos.9.12: Yea, though they rear their children, yet will I make them childless, till there be no human being,—for it is, nothing less than woe, to them when I depart from them!
texts.hos.9.13: Ephraim! just as I provided for Tyre, was planted in a meadow,—yet, Ephraim, must needs bring forth for a murderer his children.
texts.hos.9.14: Give them, O Yahweh—what wilt thou give? Give them, a miscarrying womb, and breasts dried up.
texts.hos.9.15: All their wickedness, is in Gilgal, yea, there, have I come to hate them, For the wickedness of their doings—out of my house, will I drive them forth,—no more will I love them, all their rulers, are unruly.
texts.hos.9.16: Smitten is Ephraim, their root, hath dried up, fruit, shall they not bear,—yea, though they do bring forth, yet will I slay the darlings of their womb.
texts.hos.9.17: My God will reject them, because they hearkened not unto him,—that they may become wanderers throughout the nations.
texts.hos.10.1: A luxuriant vine, is Israel, fruit, beseemeth him,—According to the abundance of his fruit, hath he brought abundance to the altars, according to the goodliness of his land, hath he made goodly statues.
texts.hos.10.2: Hypocritical is their heart, Now, shall they be held guilty,—He, will break down their altars, he will destroy their statutes.
texts.hos.10.3: For, now, will they say, We have no king,—for we revere not Yahweh, and what could, a king, do for us?
texts.hos.10.4: They have spoken words, swearing falsely, in solemnizing a covenant,—therefore shall judgment, spring up like a poisonous plant, on the ridges of the field.
texts.hos.10.5: About the calves of Beth-aven, will the inhabitant of Samaria be concerned,—for the people thereof, have mourned over it, and, the ascetics thereof, who, over it, used to exult, [shall mourn] for the glory thereof, because it hath departed therefrom.
texts.hos.10.6: Itself also, to Assyria, shall be borne along, as a present to a hostile king,—shame, shall Ephraim receive, that Israel, may be ashamed, of his own counsel.
texts.hos.10.7: Silenced is Samaria: her king, is as a chip on the face of the waters,
texts.hos.10.8: So shall the high places of Aven, be destroyed, the sin of Israel, Thorn and prickle, shall come up on their altars,—Therefore shall they say to the mountains, Cover us, and to the hills, Fall on us.
texts.hos.10.9: Beyond the days of Gibeah, hast thou sinned, O Israel: there, came they to a stand, the battle against the sons of perversity, touched them not in Gibeah.
texts.hos.10.10: When I please, then will I chastise them,—and there shall be gathered together against them—peoples, they being harnessed to their two Iniquities;
texts.hos.10.11: But, Ephraim, shall be a heifer broken in, loving to tread out corn, when, I, have passed over upon her fair neck,—I will drive Ephraim, Judah, shall plow, Jacob, shall harrow to him.
texts.hos.10.12: Sow to yourselves in righteousness, reap ye at the bidding of lovingkindness, furrow to yourselves the newly-ploughed soil,—then will be the time to seek Yahweh, until he come, that he may rain down righteousness for you.
texts.hos.10.13: Ye have plowed lawlessness, perversity, have ye reaped, ye have eaten the fruit of deception,—because thou didst trust in thy chariots, in the multitude of thy mighty men.
texts.hos.10.14: Therefore shall there arise a tumult among thy peoples, and, all thy fortresses, shall be plundered, as Shalman plundered Beth-arbel, in the day of battle,—the mother, upon her children, dashed to the ground.
texts.hos.10.15: Even so, hath Bethel, done to you, because of your exceeding wickedness,—in the dawn, shall the king of Israel be, utterly silenced.
texts.hos.11.1: When Israel was, a child, then I loved him,—and, out of Egypt, called I my son.
texts.hos.11.2: They invited them,—at once, they departed from before me, they, to the Baals, sacrificed, and, to the images, offered incense.
texts.hos.11.3: Yet, I, had taught Ephraim to walk, I used to take them upon mine arms,—But they acknowledged not that I had healed them.
texts.hos.11.4: With human cords, used I to draw them, with the bands of love, so became I unto them like those who remove the yoke [that was] on their jaws,—and, holding out [food] to him, I let him eat.
texts.hos.11.5: He was not to turn back into the land of Egypt, Howbeit, the Assyrian—he, became his king, for they refused to turn.
texts.hos.11.6: Therefore shall the sword, rage, in his cities, and make an end of his multitudes, and consume them,—because of their counsels.
texts.hos.11.7: But, my people, are bent towards turning from me, though upwards they call them, none of them can lift them.
texts.hos.11.8: How can I give thee up, Ephraim? abandon thee Israel? How can I make thee as Admah? set thee as Zeboim? Mine own heart, turneth against me, at once, are kindled my compassions.
texts.hos.11.9: I cannot execute the glow of mine anger, I cannot turn to destroy Ephraim,—for, GOD, am, I, and not man, When thou drawest near, [I am] a Holy One, though I do not enter a city.
texts.hos.11.10: After Yahweh, let them go, Like a lion, will he roar,—When, he, shall roar, then let sons, come trembling, out of the West.
texts.hos.11.11: Let them come trembling like a small bird out of Egypt, and like a dove out of the land of Assyria,—so will I cause them to dwell by their own houses, Declareth Yahweh.
texts.hos.11.12: They have compassed me about—with denial, Ephraim, with deceit, the house of Israel,—but, Judah, hath, again and again, run riot with GOD, though, with the holy places, entrusted.
texts.hos.12.1: Ephraim, feedeth on wind, and pursueth the east wind, all the day, falsehood and force, doth he magnify,—and, a covenant with Assyria, would they solemnize, and, oil into Egypt, must be borne along.
texts.hos.12.2: But, a controversy, hath Yahweh with Judah,—so that he may bring punishment on Jacob, according to his ways, According to his doings, repay him.
texts.hos.12.3: In the womb, took he his brother by the heel; and, in his manly vigour, strove he with God:
texts.hos.12.4: Yea he strove against a Messenger, and prevailed, he wept, and made supplication unto him,—At Bethel, he found him, and, there, he spake with us;
texts.hos.12.5: And, Yahweh, is God of host,—Yahweh, is his memorial.
texts.hos.12.6: Thou, therefore, by thy God, shalt return,—lovingkindness and justice, do thou keep, so wait thou for thy God, continually.
texts.hos.12.7: A trafficker! in his hand, are balances of deceit, to oppress, he loveth.
texts.hos.12.8: So then Ephraim said, Surely I have gotten me riches, I have found wealth for myself,—in all my toils, they cannot find in me perversity which is sin.
texts.hos.12.9: But, I, Yahweh, have been thy God, from the land of Egypt,—I will yet make thee dwell in tents, as in the days of appointed meeting.
texts.hos.12.10: And I will lay my word upon the prophets, yea, I myself, have magnified, vision,—and, by the hand of the prophets, will I use similitudes.
texts.hos.12.11: If, Gilead, is in sorrow, surely false, have they been, In Gilgal, have they sacrificed, bullocks,—their very altars, shall become as heaps upon the furrows of the field.
texts.hos.12.12: When Jacob fled to the country of Syria, then Israel served for a wife, and, for a wife, he watched over a flock.
texts.hos.12.13: And, by a prophet, Yahweh, brought up, Israel out of Egypt,—and, by a prophet, was he watched over.
texts.hos.12.14: Ephraim hath provoked, very bitterly,—his own blood, therefore, upon him, will he leave, and, his reproach, shall his Lord, bring back to him.
texts.hos.13.1: When Ephraim, spake, there was terror, exalted was, he, in Israel,—but, when he became guilty with Baal, then he died.
texts.hos.13.2: Now, therefore they go on to sin, and have made them a Molten Thing out of their silver, after the notion of idols, the workmanship of craftsmen, all of it! Of them, are they saying—Ye sacrificers of men! The Great Calf, shall ye surely kiss!
texts.hos.13.3: Therefore, shall they become like the morning cloud, and like the dew early departing,—like chaff storm-driven out of the threshing-floor, and like smoke out of a chimney.
texts.hos.13.4: Yet, I, Yahweh, have been thy God from the land of Egypt,—and, god beside me, shalt thou not acknowledge, for, saviour, is there none besides me.
texts.hos.13.5: I, tended thee in the desert,—in a land parched with drought:
texts.hos.13.6: Whenever they were pastured, then were they satisfied, They were satisfied, and their heart, was lifted up,—because of this, they forgat me.
texts.hos.13.7: Therefore am I become to them as a lion,—As a leopard by the way, do I watch.
texts.hos.13.8: I will fall upon them as a bear bereaved, and will read asunder the enclosure of their heart,—that I may devour them there, like a lioness, the wild beast of the field, shall tear them in pieces.
texts.hos.13.9: It hath utterly destroyed thee, O Israel, for it was against me, as thy helper!
texts.hos.13.10: Where is thy king, then, that he may save thee throughout all thy cities? and thy judges, concerning whom thou saidst, Oh give me a king and rulers?
texts.hos.13.11: I might give thee a king in mine anger, and take him away in my wrath.
texts.hos.13.12: Bound up, is the iniquity of Ephraim, stored away, his sin.
texts.hos.13.13: The pangs of a woman in labour, shall overtake him,—he, is a son, not wise, for, now, he cannot stand still, when children are about to be born.
texts.hos.13.14: Out of the hand of hades, will I ransom them, out of death, will I redeem them,—Where is thy pestilence, O death? Where thy plague, O hades? Repentance, shall be hid from mine eyes.
texts.hos.13.15: Though, he, among brethren, be fruitful, there shall come in an east wind, the blast of Yahweh out of the desert coming up, that his spring, may dry up, and his fountain, be exhausted, he, will rob the treasure-house of all the vessels of delight.
texts.hos.13.16: Samaria, shall be held guilty, for she hath rebelled against her God, By the sword, shall they fall, their infants, shall be dashed to the ground, and, his women with child, shall be ripped up.
texts.hos.14.1: Return thou, O Israel, unto Yahweh thy God,—for thou hast stumbled by thine iniquity.
texts.hos.14.2: Take with you words, and return to Yahweh: say unto him—Wholly, shalt thou take away iniquity, Accept, then, with favour, and we will make good the boldness of our lips!
texts.hos.14.3: Assyria, shall not save us, Upon horses, will we not ride, neither will we say any more—Our god! to the work of our own hands! For, in thee, shall the fatherless, find compassion.
texts.hos.14.4: I will heal their apostacy, I will love them freely,—for mine anger, hath turned, from them.
